tasks.short: Inspect instruments and equipment for damage, test for leaks, and record defects and send items for repair.

steps.what: Sterile processing technician examines equipment for worn or loose parts under magnification
Sterile processing technician tests equipment to detect leaks
Sterile processing technician records defects for repair: on paper forms today, by scanning the item and choosing the defect type after the change
Sterile processing technician checks the repair order: item, defect described, the set it leaves and the repair service it goes to
Sterile processing technician submits the checked repair order

tasks.design: Each instrument carries a scannable code in the instrument tracking system ({OPS_SYSTEM}); a defect is logged by scanning the item and choosing the defect type, which drafts the repair order and removes the item from its set list, instead of a paper form; the technician checks the order and submits it once. Inspecting and leak testing stay with the technician.
tasks.previous_blocker: Defects were written on paper forms that travelled with the instrument.
tasks.enabler_now: Instrument tracking systems log defects and repairs per item.
tasks.still_hard: Older instruments are not individually marked.
tasks.human_edge: Feeling a hinge that is starting to stiffen.

evidence.claim: Instrument tracking systems can log defects and create repair orders per marked instrument.

assumptions: Boundary: from cleaned instruments to repairs requested; the repair itself is outside.
Input contract: instruments marked with codes; fallback is paper forms.

Inspecting, testing, the order check and the submit keep their full time. s3 keeps 50 because the scan replaces writing item details and updating the set list, and the technician still records each defect.
Repair staff handle scanned orders as they did paper ones.
research_questions: Are defective instruments out of sets sooner?

incremental.description: Sterile processing technician marks unmarked instruments.

approvals.approved_version: The repair order with item, defect and set exactly as checked by the technician in s3b, submitted once to the repair service's queue; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many instruments are not yet marked, so paper forms stay for most defects and s3 keeps 80 (2.1); high: instruments marked with codes (6.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Walk the sterile storage to check expiry dates, remove outdated packs for reprocessing, and record removed packs.

steps.what: Storage staff scan each pack into its storage location at put-away
Sterile processing technician checks sterile supplies to ensure they are not outdated
Sterile processing technician removes outdated packs and returns them for reprocessing
Sterile processing technician records removed packs: on a list today, by scanning each pack out for reprocessing after the change

tasks.design: Every pack is scanned into a storage location when it is put away, so the tracking system ({OPS_SYSTEM}) lists packs due to expire per location; the technician goes straight to them instead of reading every label on every shelf. Removed packs are scanned out for reprocessing. Removing and handling packs stays with the technician.
tasks.previous_blocker: Every label on every shelf had to be read on the round.
tasks.enabler_now: Tracking systems record pack locations and expiry dates by scan.
tasks.still_hard: Packs moved without a scan go missing from the list.
tasks.human_edge: Spotting a torn wrapper that makes a pack unsterile before its date.
tasks.altitude: The technician goes to listed packs instead of reading every label.

reach.learn: Whether outdated packs reach the theatre less often.

evidence.claim: Tracking systems can record pack storage locations and expiry dates by scan.

assumptions: Boundary: from the storage round to removals recorded; reprocessing is outside.
Input contract: packs scanned at put-away; fallback is reading every label.
Packs are still checked for damage when picked.
Storage staff scan at put-away (s0p, other-role time). s1 keeps 40 for walking to the listed packs and checking them; s3 keeps 30 for scanning each pack out.
research_questions: Do outdated packs found in theatres fall?

incremental.description: Sterile processing technician corrects locations for packs moved without a scan.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many packs are moved without a scan, so locations are unreliable and s1 keeps 70 (23.9); high: packs scanned at put-away (41.8).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Run the daily sterilizer tests, read the indicators, record cycle data and test results, sign off load release, and file printouts.

steps.what: Sterile processing technician runs daily sterilizer tests and biological indicators
Sterile processing technician reads the indicator results
Sterile processing technician records cycle data: in a paper logbook today; after the change checks the data the sterilizer sent
Sterile processing technician records the indicator results: in the logbook today, on screen against the cycle after the change
Sterile processing technician checks the load before release: cycle data within limits, indicators passed, and the load list
Sterile processing technician releases the checked load in the tracking system
Sterile processing technician files cycle printouts in binders

tasks.design: Sterilizers send cycle data (time, temperature, pressure) to the tracking system ({OPS_SYSTEM}) after each cycle, and the technician enters the indicator result on screen against that cycle, so cycle data are not written in a logbook or filed as printouts. The technician checks each load and releases it once. Running tests, reading indicators and releasing loads stay with the technician.
tasks.previous_blocker: Cycle data and results were written in logbooks and printouts filed in binders.
tasks.enabler_now: Sterilizers export cycle data to tracking systems.
tasks.human_edge: Holding back a load when an indicator looks doubtful.
tasks.altitude: The technician confirms results instead of copying them.

reach.learn: Whether records are complete at audit.

evidence.claim: Sterilizers can export cycle data to tracking systems.

assumptions: Boundary: from the sterilizer cycle to printouts filed; reprocessing failed loads is outside.
Input contract: sterilizers connected; fallback is the logbook.

Load release stays with the technician: the check and the release keep their full time. Entering indicator results is still done by eye and keeps its full time; s3 keeps 10 for checking the sent cycle data.
The system is validated before paper records stop.

incremental.description: Sterile processing technician enters data from unconnected sterilizers.

approvals.approved_version: The load with its cycle data and indicator results exactly as checked by the technician in s4, released once in the tracking system for use; any failed result or change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: mostly old sterilizers without a link, so cycle data are still written and printouts filed; s3 and s5 keep 70 (8.0); high: all sterilizers connected (26.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Count supplies, record equipment usage, write orders when inventory is low, check them, send them to purchasing, and receive deliveries.

steps.what: Sterile processing technician tracks supplies: counts the shelves today, scans the barcode of each empty bin after the change
Sterile processing technician maintains records of equipment usage in a spreadsheet
Sterile processing technician writes orders for medical instruments or supplies when inventory is low
Sterile processing technician checks the final order: items and quantities against usage and coming procedures, and the purchasing account
Sterile processing technician sends the checked order to purchasing: by e-mail today, by one release in the purchasing system after the change
Sterile processing technician receives and stores deliveries

tasks.design: Supplies sit on two-bin shelves with barcodes; scanning an empty bin adds the item to an order in the purchasing system ({PROCUREMENT}), so shelves are not counted by eye. Equipment usage comes from the tracking system's scans of sets per procedure instead of a spreadsheet. The technician checks the order and releases it once to purchasing in the system. Receiving and storing deliveries stay with the technician.
tasks.previous_blocker: Shelves were counted by eye, usage kept in spreadsheets and orders typed.
tasks.enabler_now: Two-bin scanning and set tracking feed purchasing systems.
tasks.still_hard: Loan instrument sets from suppliers are tracked separately.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing a big surgery list next week needs extra sets.
tasks.altitude: The technician checks orders instead of counting and typing.

evidence.claim: Two-bin scanning and set tracking can feed purchasing systems.

assumptions: Boundary: from the stock round to the delivery stored; supplier contracts are outside.
Input contract: standing list kept by purchasing; fallback is counting and typing.
The technician checks every order. s1 keeps 50 for scanning empty bins and counting special items; s3 keeps 30 for adding special items; s5 keeps 20 for the release.
Purchasing handles system orders as they did e-mails.

incremental.description: Sterile processing technician adjusts bin sizes and reorder points.

approvals.approved_version: The order with items and quantities exactly as checked by the technician in s4, released once to purchasing in the purchasing system; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many special items stay off the bins, so s1 keeps 80 and s3 keeps 60 (32.0); high: mostly standard supplies (45.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The sterile processing technician keeps inspecting, testing and releasing loads; paper forms, logbooks, label reading and counting shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A technician with more time on inspection.
